subject: NovaSystems renewal runway: usage gaps, surge guardrails, and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prep: NovaSystems renewal health + options

Team —

Quick prep for the renewal touchpoint with Novasystems next week. Attached is a short usage pack (usage_report_Q1_2027.pdf) and a compact SLA/options sheet (sla-option-matrix.xlsx). High-level takeaways from our metrics: 

- Run rate: steady ~34M tokens/month over last 30 days, but 3x spikes from Conversational Assist window (09:00–11:00 PT) causing 95th p95 latency to move from 180ms to ~480ms.
- Token mix: 68% text-gen, 22% embeddings, 10% rerank requests. Embedding cost is high due to batch size variance.
- Cache: prefix cache hit ~22% — opportunity for prefix harmonization on user flows.
- Economics: current blended cost ~ $3.6 per 1M tokens after discounts; margin opportunity if they accept quantized variants for non-critical paths.

Possible proposal paths to discuss:
1) Standard renewal: 12-month, 1.2x current commit, standard SLA, 30% overage discount for first quarter.
2) Headroom + burst: 12-month, 1.0x commit + 200k burst credits + guaranteed burst pool for peak hours (we can offer a 10% uplift to commit pricing).
3) Performance-split: adopt q4_8 quantized model for embeddings and routing to high-perf LLM for generation during spikes; reduces token cost by ~18% (estimate).

Ask: please review the attached and call out any fatal objections by EOD tomorrow. If we're leaning toward offering a guaranteed burst pool we'll need an ops-ok for allocation and an SLA tweak (see attachment).

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: usage_report_Q1_2027.pdf (summary), sla-option-matrix.xlsx (decision matrix)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Cho <claire.cho@novasystems.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: NovaSystems — Renewal health review & flexible capacity options

Hi Claire —

Thanks for taking time to review renewal options with us. Per our internal health check, I wanted to share a short, actionable summary and three practical paths we think will address both runway (predictability) and peak performance (latency sensitivity during morning conversational shift).

Executive summary (attached: usage_report_Q1_2027.pdf):
- Current 30-day run rate: ~34M tokens/month; 3x peak windows causing p95 latency jumps to ~480ms.
- Cost baseline: current effective cost ~ $3.6 per 1M tokens; we see 12–18% unit savings by moving embedding jobs onto a quantized variant + batching improvements.

Options we recommend (one pager attached: sla-option-matrix.xlsx):
A) Commit uplift (1.2x) — simplest path for predictable unit economics. Includes standard renewal terms and a one-time onboarding credit to help smoothing migration.
B) Headroom + Burst pool — keep commit at ~current run rate (1.0x) and add 200k burst credits and a reserved burst pool during 08:00–12:00 PT windows to protect p95 latency. This keeps flexibility with limited financial commitment.
C) Split-model performance plan — route embeddings to q4_8 quantized variant and generation to our high-perf instance at peak hours (best for controlling cost and latency).

Questions for you: which of these aligns best with Novasystems' procurement timeline and internal runway expectations? If helpful we can run a simulation for projected cost and p95 impact for each option.

Next steps: if you approve a preferred option we will: (1) nail down exact commit numbers, (2) lock SLA language for burst guardrails, and (3) schedule a short operational cutoff review with Marcus to confirm provisioning windows.

Looking forward —
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0187

Attachments: usage_report_Q1_2027.pdf, sla-option-matrix.xlsx

From: Claire Cho <claire.cho@novasystems.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Novasystems Procurement <procurement@novasystems.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovaSystems — Renewal health review & flexible capacity options

Jordan —

Thanks for the crisp summary. A few quick clarifying Qs before we pull procurement in: 
1) For option B (Headroom + Burst) — how are burst credits consumed and replenished? Is there an expiry?
2) For option C — what is the expected impact on embedding fidelity with q4_8? We have a small set of downstream ranking tests that are sensitive.
3) Procurement: our legal needs a sample SLA sentence for guaranteed burst pool and p95 commitment during the 08:00–12:00 PT window. Can you provide that text?

Timeline: we are aiming to finalize commercial terms by 2027-03-24 (end of month for finance window). If we can get a short simulation and the SLA language by Friday 2027-03-12, procurement will be able to prep a PO draft.

Also — we noticed a couple of outlier jobs that generate very large single-request embeddings. Can Redwood advise on batching suggestions?

Best,
Claire
Claire Cho
Director, Platform Engineering — Novasystems

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prep: NovaSystems renewal health + options (internal)

Looping in an ops/engineering angle and the commercial concession ask from Claire. My suggested responses below: 

1) Burst credits lifecycle: propose 200k credits allocated up-front, usable for 12 months; unconsumed credits expire at term end. Consumption is first-in-first-out against burst pool and only recharges on renewal. We reserve the right to deny sustained draining that breaches safety thresholds (we'll tie to a 24-hour moving average cap).

2) Embedding fidelity on q4_8: Marcus — can you run the ranking test set and provide delta (mean reciprocal rank + accuracy) by EOD Thursday? We should quantify the negative delta; if <1.2% accuracy drop we can push C as low-risk with cost upside.

3) SLA sample text (draft): "Redwood will provide a reserved burst pool for Novasystems during 08:00–12:00 PT with a p95 latency target not to exceed 300ms for routed generation requests when burst pool is engaged. In the event of sustained saturation beyond the burst allocation, Redwood will provide prioritized routing and surge mitigation; such events will be identified in the Console and remediated per standard incident escalation."

4) Commercial concession: suggest offering a 10% price uplift on committed unit pricing (so effectively larger discount vs metered) for the first quarter OR a one-time 30% overage credit for first 90 days. Which is less impactful from finance perspective? Karthik?

If Marcus can share the embedding delta and Ops can sign-off on the burst pool safety cap, I'm happy to send a revised commercial proposal + SLA text to Claire by Friday morning.

-J

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Cho <claire.cho@novasystems.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Novasystems Procurement <procurement@novasystems.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovaSystems — Renewal health review & flexible capacity options — proposed path forward

Claire —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the timeline note. Per internal checks: Marcus ran the ranking delta (summary below) and Ops signed off on the burst safety caps. Final proposal follows.

Embedding fidelity (Marcus Lin): q4_8 delta on your ranking suite = 0.7% MRR degradation, no statistically significant drop on top-10 accuracy. Recommendation: safe to pilot for embeddings with canary routing for 20% of traffic.

Burst pool & SLA (Ops): approved. Finalized terms: 200k burst credits allocated at term start, usable for 12 months, 08:00–12:00 PT reserved pool with preemption priority for Novasystems. Safety cap: if 24-hour consumption rate > 2.5x average run-rate, Redwood reserves temporary throttling and will notify within 1 hour. SLA sample clause attached.

Commercial offer (summary):
- Term: 12 months starting 2027-04-01
- Commit: 1.5x current average monthly run rate (agreed to protect runway)
- Burst: 200k credits (12-month expiry)
- Intro concession: one-time 30% overage credit applied to first 90 days to ease transition
- Pricing note: committed unit price will be adjusted per the attached matrix; effective blended price projected to be ~ $3.1 per 1M tokens for first quarter.

Next steps: if this aligns, we'll (A) send a commercial addendum for signature (we can provision a PO reference from procurement), (B) schedule a 30-min ops cutover next week to configure the reserved burst pool, and (C) run a 2-week q4_8 canary for embeddings. 

If procurement wants a redline-ready clause for the burst pool SLA I'll attach the sentence we drafted.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a brief call if you'd prefer to walk through.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0187

Attachments: usage_report_Q1_2027.pdf, sla-option-matrix.xlsx
